summary: Rename account_user.note to customer_note with zero downtime: add new column, backfill data, deploy new version state-only, create a bidirectional database sync trigger, retire old version, and drop old column, ensuring both apps see consistent data throughout.
write_consistency: A PostgreSQL AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE trigger synchronises note and customer_note: on each insert or update, the column not explicitly set by the app is filled from the other column using COALESCE or DISTINCT-aware assignment, so that a write from one version is immediately visible to the other version via a read of the other column. During concurrent traffic both columns hold identical values, guaranteeing consistent reads.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed because it relied on separate columns with no synchronisation mechanism while both app versions ran concurrently. Old app writes to note, new app writes to customer_note, but writes from one version were not reflected in the other column, causing the deterministic checks (old_write_new_read, new_write_old_read, column agreement, preservation counts) to fail. This revised plan adds a database trigger that bi-directionally copies the written value to the other column on INSERT/UPDATE, ensuring data parity during concurrent operation. The trigger is created before the new version starts serving traffic (in the expand stage), so sync is in effect from deploy_new onward. Additionally, SQL strings were restructured as single-statement strings with proper dollar-quoting to avoid PostgreSQL syntax errors such as 'syntax error at or near ";"' and 'syntax error at end of input'.

stages.description: Add customer_note column and create sync trigger
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_user_note_trig() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN NEW.customer_note := COALESCE(NEW.customer_note, NEW.note); NEW.note := COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note); ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; END IF; IF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; RETURN NEW; END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_user_note_after_insert_update AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_user_note_trig();

stages.description: Copy note values into customer_note for rows that have a note
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL AND note IS NOT NULL;

stages.description: Deploy new-staged version with state-only Django migration; new app now writes customer_note, old app still writes note
Retire the old version; after this stage only the new version serves traffic against the database.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note CASCADE;
